doc: A history, as saved by an application's history_output: the map is rebuilt from it. A surface's (isotropic_remeshing, qslim, shortest_edge_collapse, tetwild, simwild) or curves' (triwild); the file says which.

transfer: the surface the history starts from -- the same triangles in the same order: a gmsh file, with per-face and per-corner fields (labels, texture coordinates) to carry onto the output, or a triangle mesh of another format, as read, with none. Empty: the input files of the application that recorded the history, from its parameters. Every output face gets input_face too, the input face its centroid maps to.
transfer: the output surface, written as a gmsh file with the carried per-face fields.
transfer: also write the output as a textured Wavefront OBJ, with uv_field as its texture coordinates and a material mapping `texture`. Empty: not written.
transfer: the per-corner field output_obj takes its texture coordinates from (its first two components).
transfer: the image the material of output_obj maps.
Directory where the input files are located. This is injected by the application and should not be set by the user.

info: build the map and report what it holds, where it stops being a bijection, and how far the output's face centroids (segment midpoints, for curves) move when mapped to the input and back. transfer (surfaces): carry every per-face field of `input` onto the output surface and write it to `output`. map: map the points of the file `points` to the output (direction to_output) or back to the input (to_input), and write them to `output_points`. features (curves): write the input's feature points -- curve ends, junctions, input points -- to `output_points`, one `input_vertex output_vertex` per line: a vertex of the input files (the curve files' vertices, in order, then the point files', from 0) and the output vertex it ended at, -1 for none.
Logs are not just printed on the terminal but also saved in this file.

transfer: the tet mesh (gmsh) the history's application wrote, whose tracked surface is where the history ends. With output_tet_mesh, the fields are written onto it: a copy of it, with the tracked surface as triangles on its own nodes carrying the fields.
transfer: where to write tet_mesh with the fields on its tracked surface.

map: a text file of points, one per line, numbers separated by blanks, '#' starting a comment. On the input (direction to_output): `face b0 b1 b2`, a triangle of the input files -- the triangles of all of them, in order, as the files hold them, from 0 -- and barycentric coordinates with respect to its corners in file order. On the output (direction to_input): `face b0 b1 b2`, a triangle of the output file, for an application whose output is a surface (isotropic_remeshing); `v0 v1 v2 b0 b1 b2`, three vertices of the output tet mesh at the corners of a tracked face, in any order, with barycentric coordinates in that order, for one whose output is a tet mesh (tetwild, simwild). On curves (triwild): `segment b0 b1` on the input, a segment of the input curve files -- the segments of all of them, in order, a polyline's consecutive vertex pairs, from 0 -- with barycentric coordinates with respect to its ends in file order; `v0 v1 b0 b1` on the output, two vertices of the output mesh at the ends of a tracked edge, in either order, with barycentric coordinates in that order.

map: where to write the mapped points, one line per point of `points`, in the same order: on the output as described for `points` (to_output), on the input as `face b0 b1 b2`, or `segment b0 b1` for curves (to_input). A point with no image has the id -1. features: where to write the feature points.
map: to_output maps points on the input to the output; to_input maps points on the output back to the input, the inverse map.

How the map follows a vertex smoothing step. flatten: the vertex's star before and after the move is flattened jointly, so points stay where they were on the surface, at one SLIM solve per move; on curves, points keep their place along the curve, by arc length. barycentric: points keep their face (segment) and barycentric coordinates, riding along with the vertex by at most its step, at no cost, as BijectiveRemesh does.

The scaffold of each local map's joint flattening, which keeps the outline the two patches share a simple polygon while SLIM lowers their distortion. box: the region between the outline and a box three times the patch, triangulated anew before every iteration, as in BijectiveRemesh; it follows the patch wherever the flattening takes it. ring: one ring of triangles out to a fixed copy of the outline; about 2.4 times faster, but it pulls the outline back and keeps it from stretching, so local maps are more distorted.
